sources.title: Nonlinear Least-Squares Approach to Frequency Estimation and Detection for Sinusoidal Signals with Arbitrary Envelope
sources.publication_status: Publisher-indexed regular journal article with citation and DOI; peer-review process not independently verified in this run.
sources.access_level: Publisher-indexed abstract only; direct publisher page returned HTTP 403
sources.content_locator: Abstract: for a sinusoid with constant or unknown time-varying amplitude, the nonlinear least-squares criterion can be minimized over amplitude/envelope to leave a periodogram-like frequency criterion. The paper also reports a statistical test for amplitude time variation based on the difference between two frequency estimates, and consistent estimates under both hypotheses.

findings.claim: A time-varying amplitude need not force frequency estimation into a Doppler-spread or frequency-drift model: for the paper's single sinusoid with unknown real envelope and additive disturbance, a nonlinear least-squares treatment profiles out the envelope and leaves a periodogram-like frequency criterion; the paper also tests for amplitude variation using a difference between two frequency estimates.
findings.support_locator: Publisher abstract at S6, retrieved in op08; direct page access status check op11 failed with HTTP 403, so no full-text methods or performance details were inspected.
findings.decision_implication: This supplies a plausible alternative discriminator for ramping or interrupted-amplitude pilot windows: compare the existing constant-amplitude block fit with an envelope-tolerant/profile fit on identical clean and ramped captures, recording error tails, presence false admissions, and computation. The amplitude-variation test could be evaluated as a way to choose which fit assumptions apply, without granting any additional signal authority.
findings.incremental_vs_seed: Adds an explicit model and estimator path for unknown time-varying amplitude, distinct from the seed's stationary tone and Doppler-spread/multiplicative-noise evidence. H05 says the current fit assumes constant amplitude within each row, while H06 includes generated helper ramps; this lead could change whether ramped rows should be excluded, segmented, or estimated with an envelope nuisance model. It does not show the proposed receiver benefits or that payload/auxiliary activity is a real-valued envelope.
findings.assumptions: Single sinusoid, real unknown envelope, and the paper's additive disturbance model are reasonable approximations over selected pilot windows; candidate algorithms can be compared with matched sample support.
findings.applicability_gap: The result is available only at publisher-abstract level. It is an asymptotic statistical statement with numerical examples, not demonstrated performance at the task's SNR, offsets, sample rates, 6-second deadline, capture chunk sizes, or absent-tone definition. A real-valued envelope model does not cover arbitrary auxiliary tones, modulation, phase resets, or multiple components. Peer review was not independently verified.
findings.next_discriminator: Using matched reference captures, compare constant-amplitude periodogram/block fitting to an envelope-profiled frequency estimate on stationary and known ramped pilot windows. Include absent-tone and auxiliary-activity controls; measure acquisition errors and nonpublications, false admissions, and work per update. Separately test whether a two-frequency-estimate amplitude-change statistic tracks injected envelope changes without vetoing valid frequency publications.

rejected_or_redundant.reason: The seed already has threshold/outlier, Kay, and differential-phase leads. Searches did not find a receiver-specific calibration or a stronger basis for translating C/N0 and dwell to the proposed target.

rejected_or_redundant.reason: The accessible abstract reports detection probability at fixed false-alarm probability for periodic pilot/code correlation. Its reference-code, periodicity, and acquisition model differ from the supplied frequency-only helper excerpts; it motivates matched detection reporting but does not settle this receiver's test.

rejected_or_redundant.item: Treating 24/30 dB-Hz, 0.10 Hz, six seconds, or 95% as empirically supported
rejected_or_redundant.reason: These remain hypothetical planning values; no located source maps them to this signal or implementation.

unresolved: Whether an envelope-profiled criterion is feasible within the actual bounded update/workspace budget; no implementation or timing was examined.
Whether helper payload or auxiliary activity can be represented as an unknown real amplitude envelope over a clean frequency aperture; source excerpts and paper model do not establish equivalence.
Receiver-specific error tails, threshold behavior, presence/absence calibration, and chunk/reset continuity remain to be measured in the engineering assignment.
The seed's source and provenance limitations remain: its cited works are summarized at abstract or metadata level in places, and publication metadata alone does not verify peer review.
retained_seed_summary: The frozen seed supports cautious treatment of single-tone threshold/outlier behavior; a light block/Kay-like estimator as a matched baseline; delay-dependent differential-phase tradeoffs conditional on phase continuity; and separate stationary versus time-varying comparisons. It recommends measuring empirical error tails, acquisition/nonpublication, false admissions, reset/chunk effects, and controlled drift. Its target values are hypothetical. Its sources S1-S5 and original claims remain as recorded below; the seed source access limits and three failed publisher opens are retained, and peer-review labels were not independently established.
